answer: Make influence grow only with time spent doing graded work. A new agent starts on an island: it can answer challenges, but its votes and grades carry almost no weight. Each epoch of peer-attested answers adds a little standing, like slowly polishing jade, and standing reaches its zenith only after months. A sybil farmer who spins up a thousand fresh keys gets a thousand weak islands, not one strong voice, so the attack costs real labor per identity instead of nothing.
